improvement_decomposition.note: Exact multiplicative decomposition of the 104.78 -> 26.95 improvement.

step1_ptq_q2k_init_plus_9th_skip_layer.caveat: Two changes at once (init mode AND the 9th skip-layer). Not separable without a further run.

true_cost_of_2bit.note: The quantization cost is best measured as QAT against the fp16 model trained on identical data, rather than against the unadapted base model.
true_cost_of_2bit.vs_unadapted_fp16_raw: 26.9519 / 21.3708 = 1.26x worse (flattered by the QAT model's domain adaptation; not the comparison to quote)

analysis.size_caveat: The QAT Q2_K file is 495.2 MB against PTQ's 479.8 MB (+3.2%), since the QAT export holds 9 skip-layers at F16. Both variants carry the same F16 tied embedding as of 2026-08-04 (see scripts/quantize_ptq.sh), so the two artifacts are closely size-matched. Describing them as identical in size and speed remains an approximation; the skip-layer allocation accounts for the residual difference.
analysis.leakage_check: qat/data.py load_wikitext2_train_examples uses split='train'; the eval corpus is split='test'. No train/eval overlap.

domain_alignment_caveat.note: Relevant when quoting any figure in this file. The QAT models train on a WikiText-2 train blend and are scored on WikiText-2 test. There is no split leakage, but the domains match, so these scores partly measure domain alignment. results/c4_perplexity.json re-runs four of these checkpoints on an off-domain C4 slice.
domain_alignment_caveat.what_changes: The blend-vs-Alpaca-only spread narrows from 2.63x here (26.95 against 70.88) to 1.31x on C4 (55.95 against 73.03), and the best QAT model moves from 1.26x worse than fp16 here to 1.90x worse on C4. Roughly half the blend's apparent advantage is domain alignment.
domain_alignment_caveat.what_holds: QAT outperforms PTQ by 8.68x on C4, so the central 2-bit QAT-vs-PTQ result holds off-domain.

bit_annealing_evaluation.note: The qat_q2k_affine_noanneal control run measured the progressive 4->2 bit-annealing schedule as making no significant difference at 1000 steps.
bit_annealing_evaluation.verdict: Statistically a no-op. The confidence intervals [26.732, 27.171] and [26.686, 27.124] overlap across almost their entire width, and the gap (0.047) is roughly a fifth of a single run's stderr, so disabling annealing carries no measured cost. The control also matters methodologically: the SEQ runs disable annealing, so without it their difference from the headline run would have combined two changes.

seq_evaluation.note: ParetoQ SEQ (--quant-function seq) evaluated against affine at matched settings (both fixed 2-bit, so the quant function is the only difference).
seq_evaluation.verdict: Not a demonstrated improvement. SEQ is nominally 0.31 lower, but the CIs overlap ([26.378, 26.810] against [26.686, 27.124]). llama-perplexity's stderr is also a within-run estimate over chunks and does not capture seed-to-seed variance between two separate training runs, so the true uncertainty on this comparison is wider than the intervals suggest. Read as a tie. The paper's claimed 2-bit advantage over LSQ-style quantization is neither reproduced nor refuted here.
seq_evaluation.init_sensitivity: SEQ is highly sensitive to shadow-weight init: 39.67 with ptq_q2k against 26.594 with roundtrip, a 1.49x swing from the init mode alone with everything else identical. Reading the ptq_q2k number in isolation would attribute that gap to SEQ itself, whereas it is a property of the init pairing. ParetoQ initializes from fp weights, which roundtrip approximates and ptq_q2k does not.
seq_evaluation.export_penalty: SEQ's Q2_K round-trip error on a sampled tensor is higher than affine's (3.03% against 1.46%), but end-to-end the proxy->GGUF degradation is nearly identical (SEQ 29.85->39.67 = 1.33x; affine 19.64->26.91 = 1.37x). The export path does not penalize SEQ disproportionately.

wasserstein_evaluation.note: Sliced-Wasserstein + MSE hidden-state block alignment (arXiv:2601.07878, --distill-loss wasserstein) evaluated against CAKLD as the distillation objective. Concluded: neither the initial run nor the scale-matched sweep improved on CAKLD, and no further variations are planned for this project.
wasserstein_evaluation.verdict: CAKLD is the better objective. The best Wasserstein result is 27.4029 (distill-weight 0.05) against CAKLD's 26.9519. The intervals [27.179, 27.627] and [26.732, 27.171] are adjacent and do not overlap, making this a real but small margin.
wasserstein_evaluation.monotone_trend: Quality degrades monotonically as the Wasserstein weight rises (27.40 -> 28.05 -> 30.71). The best tested weight is the smallest one, so within the range tested the term is a net negative at every setting. A distill-weight 0 point was not run, so this establishes that quality decreases in weight across the three measured points rather than that the optimum is at zero.

weight_scale_confound.initial_weight_mismatch: The first Wasserstein run reused CAKLD's --distill-weight 0.5. This is not a controlled swap: the Wasserstein term is an unnormalized hidden-state MSE whose natural magnitude (kd_loss ~19-23) is an order of magnitude larger than CAKLD's KL-in-nats (kd_loss ~0.8-1.9). At the same nominal weight it took 69-74% of the total loss where CAKLD takes 10-20%, roughly a 5x shift in the task/distillation balance. That run therefore measured Wasserstein-dominated training against CAKLD as a mild regularizer, rather than the two objectives head to head.
weight_scale_confound.resolution: Re-ran at distill-weight 0.05 and 0.1, bringing the Wasserstein share to 13% and 31%; 0.05 lands inside CAKLD's 10-20% band. With the scale matched, Wasserstein still scores above CAKLD, so the result is not an artifact of the weight.
weight_scale_confound.guidance: --distill-weight is not comparable across --distill-loss choices. Any future distillation objective added to this repo should have its loss share checked against CAKLD's 10-20% before its weight is treated as equivalent.

wasserstein_evaluation.export_penalty: proxy -> GGUF degradation is 1.42x for Wasserstein dw=0.5 and 1.37x for CAKLD, so the export path does not disadvantage Wasserstein; its deficit is present in training.
wasserstein_evaluation.run_health: All four Wasserstein runs (100-step crash-check plus three 1000-step runs) completed with zero non-finite loss/gradient events and zero skipped updates. kd_loss started well above zero (22.95) and fell monotonically to 9.14, confirming the student was quantized and the objective was optimizing. Gradient norms at dw=0.5 were high (157 falling to 29, against ~10-50 for CAKLD), consistent with the loss-scale imbalance, and normalized at the lower weights.

seq_alpha_positivity.note: Identified while verifying that SEQ's learnable alpha trains. Fixed in commit ea51fe2.
seq_alpha_positivity.observed: After 1000 steps, 3 of 26,279,936 alpha scales had gone non-positive (min -3.0e-05). The count did not grow between step 100 and step 1000, and no run produced a NaN.
seq_alpha_positivity.why_it_matters: alpha < 0 mirrors a group's quantization grid without raising an error; alpha == 0 makes the backward's W_Q/alpha term 0/0 = NaN, which the |u| < 1 indicator cannot mask because nan * 0 == nan.
seq_alpha_positivity.fix: abs().clamp_min(_EPS) on alpha in seq_fake_quant -- an exact identity for every alpha > _EPS, so all measured SEQ results above remain reproducible from the fixed code (verified bit-identical forward for positive alpha).
seq_alpha_positivity.alpha_training_behavior: All 187 alpha tensors moved; mean relative change 0.14% at 100 steps, growing by 1000 steps (largest mover layers.16.mlp.up_proj at 2.02%). Alpha trains rather than remaining at init.

batch24_fineweb_scaleup.note: Full-scale run (48828 steps, ~600M tokens, batch 24, lr 2.5e-5) testing whether reducing WikiText-2's share of the training blend (0.5 -> 0.05) and adding general-domain FineWeb data (0.5 share, see qat/data.py module docstring for why FineWeb over RedPajama/SlimPajama) generalizes better than the prior WikiText-heavy recipe Motivated by the prior recipe's ~119x repetition of the 2.5M-token WikiText-2 train corpus at this token budget being a memorization risk.
batch24_fineweb_scaleup.result: Both eval sets improved over the prior best (qat_q2k_blend): WikiText2 26.9519 -> 18.4863 (-31.4% relative), C4 55.9509 -> 32.2462 (-42.4% relative). The C4 (held-out, non-domain-matched) improvement is larger than the WikiText2 one, which is the outcome this run was designed to test: the gain reflects generalization from the more diverse data mix rather than domain-alignment inflation.
batch24_fineweb_scaleup.training_time_proxy_note: The in-training (truncated, 20k-token) WikiText2 ppl proxy bottomed at step ~19,200 (~13.07) then drifted upward to 14.30 by the final step 48828 -- a gradual drift rather than noise, plausibly from the ~12-13x repetition of this run's data pool late in training. The step-20,000 safety-net checkpoint, which would have allowed testing whether that trough held up under the full llama-perplexity/GGUF measurement, was not available: --save-every checkpoints before this run's fix (see git log, 'Fix safety-net checkpoint overwrite') wrote to a fixed filename, so each save replaced the previous one, leaving only the step-47500 save at the end of training.
batch24_fineweb_scaleup.step47500_comparison: Step 47500, the other surviving checkpoint, was measured against both eval sets as the closest available substitute: WikiText2 18.6311 +/- 0.1531 and C4 32.4342 +/- 0.2859, both statistically indistinguishable from the final checkpoint's 18.4863 +/- 0.1512 / 32.2462 +/- 0.2837 (overlapping stderr intervals). On the full measurement, the late-training drift visible in the training-time proxy did not appear as a meaningful difference between these two points 1328 steps apart, and both improve substantially on the prior recipe. Whether the step-19,200 trough would have measured lower than either is not determinable for this run; the checkpoint-overwrite behaviour is fixed for future ones.
batch24_fineweb_scaleup.conclusion: Promote qat_q2k_fineweb_final as the current best on both WikiText2 and C4, replacing qat_q2k_blend. There is no basis to prefer the step-47500 checkpoint over it. No 'beats fp16' claim is made from this result: see results/c4_perplexity.json's analysis.batch24_fineweb_scaleup.fp16_ceiling_status for the reasoning, and .fineweb_c4_overlap for the FineWeb/C4 content-overlap check performed before adopting it.
